title: Context Engineering: Managing Context and Memory
why: Our chat calls tools and streams, but on the second question it no longer remembers the first: the model is stateless. Today we see what goes to the model in every request and who decides it — we do. We store the conversation history in PostgreSQL, the tool messages included, and send the model only what it needs, so that the cost and the context don't grow with every question. With agents this becomes the key skill.
outcomes: You'll explain what goes into the model's context (System, tools, history, tool results, the question) and how context engineering differs from prompt engineering
You'll store the conversation history in PostgreSQL: a `conversationId`, the whole `ChatMessage` in jsonb, the tool messages included
You'll write `/chat` with a history: load → System + history + question → store `response.Messages`
You'll explain why the tokens grow with every question, and send only the last N messages into the context with `MessageCountingChatReducer`

review.q: Why doesn't the model remember the previous question, and how do we “remind” it?
review.a: The model is stateless: it only sees this request · we send the history in every request — the memory is in our code, not in the model

review.q: What goes into the context, and which part grows fastest?
review.a: System + the tool descriptions + the history + the tool results + the new question · often the tool results (e.g. the whole menu), which stay in the history

review.q: Why do we store the whole `ChatMessage` in jsonb and not a Text column?
review.a: `Contents` has different types: text, functionCall, functionResult, the thought signature · `AIJsonUtilities.DefaultOptions` stores them with `$type` · jsonb reorders keys → `AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties`

review.q: Why don't we store the System prompt in the database?
review.a: It's ours, not part of the conversation: it has today's date in it and the rules may change · we build it again on every request and put it at the top of the list

review.q: What does `MessageCountingChatReducer(10)` do, and what stays in the database?
review.a: It keeps the last 10 messages in the context and drops the tool messages · everything stays in the database · the model gets the price again with a tool

quiz.q: On the second question (“And at 21:00?”) the model doesn't know what it's about. Why?
options: The model is stateless: the first question wasn't in the second request
quiz.explain: The model only sees what we sent in this request. We send the history.

options: Deciding what to put in the model's context on every request, what to leave out and in what order
quiz.explain: Prompt engineering — how to write the instruction; context engineering — what goes into the window as a whole.

quiz.q: Why don't we store the history in a `Dictionary` in a Singleton service?
options: It disappears when the app restarts, and with two servers one user would have different memories
A Dictionary is forbidden in a Singleton
quiz.explain: In the database the history stays and every server sees the same one.

quiz.q: Why do we store the whole `ChatMessage` in one jsonb column?
options: `Contents` are parts of different types (text, functionCall, functionResult…) — splitting them into columns is a dead end
EF Core can't store any other type
quiz.explain: AIJsonUtilities.DefaultOptions writes every part with a $type, so the right type is created when reading back.

quiz.q: What do we need `AllowOutOfOrderMetadataProperties = true` for?
options: jsonb reorders keys and `$type` is no longer first — without it reading throws an exception
quiz.explain: By default System.Text.Json expects $type to be first in the object.

quiz.q: In `/chat`, what do we store with `AppendAsync`?
options: The System prompt, the question and the answer
The question and `response.Messages` — the tool request, the result and the answer
quiz.explain: We store everything that happened in the conversation. The System prompt is ours and gets built again every time.

quiz.q: InputTokenCount grows with every question in a conversation. What is NOT a consequence of this?
options: The context window fills up sooner or later
The model learns something new and gets smarter
quiz.explain: The model learns nothing (lecture 1) — it just reads more, and we pay more.

quiz.q: After `MessageCountingChatReducer(10)`, what does the model do on a price question if the menu is no longer in the context?
options: It calls `get_menu` again and gets the new price
quiz.explain: The reducer drops the tool messages — the model calls a tool again when it needs to, and the price is fresh.
